narrative.overview: Every conflict of 2000 to 2026 passes through one room: the UN Security Council. The shell borrows that room's world and nothing of its branding. The map is the table. The HUD is the chamber's deep council blue. Every country that acts in the game sits behind a delegate's nameplate, its placard. The topology is Hearts of Iron IV's, exactly, because the players already know it. The world supplies type, palette, density and one signature move, the placard, and never the layout. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and the font's width axis alone. There is no grain, bevel, gradient, glow or corner tick anywhere. The map is printed in an atlas tone (country colours slightly desaturated and settled toward navy) on a chart-blue sea, so the white placards and the resolution blue stay the brightest things on screen during long evening sessions.
keyCharacteristics: Opaque council-navy panels on 1px blue hairlines; square corners everywhere.
Resolution blue marks selection, progress, the active tab and focus. Placard white marks a country holding the floor, finished work and the primary action.
Wide capitals for titles and placards; condensed tabular figures for numbers; a serif document voice for narrative text.
Green, red and amber appear only on values that are good, bad or at risk.
A rich tooltip on every number, tile and row.

rules.name: The Vote Board Rule
rules.body: Green (good), red (bad) and amber (warn) appear only on values that are actually improving, worsening or at risk, such as stat flashes, approval, and Security Council votes. Never as decoration.

rules.name: The Data Colour Rule
rules.body: Party, ideology and country colours come from the game data. Swatches, flags, war-score bars and unit symbols show them as they are. The map alone renders them through the uniform atlas tone, a presentation step that never changes the data.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue means "selected or in progress" and white means "holding the floor or done". Do not use either for emphasis that carries neither meaning.

rules.name: The Heading-First Rule
rules.body: A name or heading leads, and its role, office or date follows beneath it. No small label sits above a heading.

rules.name: The Fit Rule
rules.body: A long country name narrows on the width axis to fit its plate (from 118% down to 75%) instead of being cut.

rules.name: The No-Ornament Rule
rules.body: No grain, bevels, gradients, glows, corner ticks or textures. A surface is flat navy or a flat plate; the only line is a 1px hairline.

dos: Do put every new system in its HOI4 position: its tab in the top row, its panel on the left, lists in the outliner, map overlays in the map-mode cluster.
Do give every number a tooltip that explains where it comes from.
Do show unbuilt systems honestly, with the phase that adds them.
Do use the authored icon set (24px grid, 1.6 stroke) for any new icon, including steppers and arrows.
Do set a country in an actor role on a placard; turn it up only for the player's country, the selection or the winner.
Do keep the top bar fitting from 1280px wide; nothing hangs below it.
Do make child components that read live game state subscribe to the clock (`version.value`).
donts: Don't round corners, or add grain, bevels, gradients, glows, glass, or gradient text.
Don't place small labels or eyebrows above headings, or coloured side stripes on cards and list items.
Don't use Unicode glyphs (▲ ▼ × + −) as icons.
Don't use Paradox-owned art, icons, fonts or textures, or the UN's emblem and name as decoration.
Don't decorate with loaded political or military symbols.
